title: Same Answer, Different Representations: Hidden instability in VLMs
abstract: arXiv:2602.06652v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The robustness of Vision Language Models (VLMs) is commonly assessed through output-level invariance, implicitly assuming that stable predictions reflect stable multimodal processing. In this work, we argue that this assumption is insufficient. We introduce a representation-aware and frequency-aware evaluation framework that measures internal embedding drift, spectral sensitivity, and structural smoothness (spatial consistency of vision tokens), alongside standard label-based metrics. Applying this framework to modern VLMs across the SEEDBench, MMMU, and POPE datasets reveals three distinct failure modes. First, models frequently preserve predicted answers while undergoing substantial internal representation drift; for perturbations such as text overlays, this drift approaches the magnitude of inter-image variability, indicating that representations move to regions typically occupied by unrelated inputs despite unchanged outputs. translated_title: 相同答案，不同表示：视觉语言模型中的隐藏不稳定性
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLMs）的鲁棒性通常通过输出层面的不变性来评估，这隐含地假设稳定的预测反映了稳定的多模态处理。在本工作中，我们认为这一假设是不充分的。我们引入了一个表示感知且频率感知的评估框架，该框架在标准标签指标之外，还测量内部嵌入漂移、频谱敏感性以及结构平滑度（视觉token的空间一致性）。将该框架应用于现代VLMs在SEEDBench、MMMU和POPE数据集上的实验揭示了三种不同的失败模式。首先，模型经常在保持预测答案不变的同时经历显著的内部表示漂移；对于文本叠加等扰动，这种漂移接近图像间变异的量级，表明尽管输出未变，表示已移动到通常被无关输入占据的区域。
tldr: 该论文提出一个表示感知且频率感知的评估框架，揭示视觉语言模型即使输出答案保持稳定，其内部表示也可能发生显著漂移，表明仅依赖输出层面的不变性评估不足以衡量模型的真实鲁棒性。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a representation-aware and frequency-aware evaluation framework revealing that VLMs can undergo substantial internal representation drift while maintaining unchanged outputs, demonstrating that output-level invariance alone is insufficient for assessing model robustness.
